name: Passionflower
short: A systematic review of nine short clinical trials (up to 30 days) observed no adverse effects. In one small trial, job-performance impairment was less common than with oxazepam.
text: A systematic review of nine clinical trials of Passiflora incarnata in adults, lasting from one day up to 30 days, reported that no adverse effects, including memory loss or collapse of psychometric functions, were observed. In a 4-week pilot randomised trial in 36 outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder, significantly more problems relating to impairment of job performance were encountered with the comparison medicine oxazepam than with passionflower extract. These were short trials. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
